# Source-owned binary body delivery feasibility

Evidence grade at assessment: Source-inspected / Device-observed baseline fallback.
This preserves the original Release3e65ae94 assessment; it is not a description
of the later production delivery state. Evaluation closed only the Plan's
assessment task. Negotiated Mihon sealed source bodies and Venera transform
outputs were subsequently implemented and scoped-verifiable; current evidence
is in the Mihon sealed-body, Venera transform-output, runtime-body Binder and
Dart-consumer lifetime audits. The nine actual Dart channel/file cases are
verified independently; full HTTP/Pipeline teardown, live pipe/stream, host input and
canonical whole bytes, nonempty Cookie/POST and performance remain open.

## Baseline production facts

The normal minified Release3e65ae94, PID23850, opens a real103-page WNACG
chapter through the normal source browser/details/Reader routes. Eight origin
reads return200 through `runtime-transform`, totaling20288603 bytes. The first
page frame appears4197666us after mount,7267413us before the first control tap.
The current page's origin open takes3929501us; its source plan takes32631us,
and its completed read precedes the first frame by186536us. This does not
separate upstream connect, header wait, transfer or source-interceptor costs.

The source returns HTTP `img5.wnimg2.cfd` page and `t4.wnimg2.cfd` cover
locators. No URL rewrite, source setting change or whitelist expansion occurs.
These current mirrors do not exercise the historical `.ru` trigger. The request
is GET with source-produced headers and no Cookie/body in this sample.

The installed WNACG1.6.0 payload adds response/mirror/compression interceptors
to the canonical client. A serialized image request alone does not prove that
replaying it with a different client preserves those behaviors.

Relevant baseline source, inspected with CodeGraph before targeted reads:

- `MihonRuntimeDriver.kt:861`: the source client owns `newCall/execute`;
  `loadResource` consumes `responseBody.bytes()` and closes the response in
  `finally`. Its result is a complete encoded `ByteArray`.
- `runtime_source_adapter.dart:947`: controlled requests are not coalesced with
  another task's runtime Future. `_loadResource` expects a complete `Uint8List`.
- `RuntimeServiceWire.kt:81`: large IPC packets already use an authenticated,
  app-private packet file. That file contains a StandardMessageCodec envelope;
  it is not a standalone image body. `read` validates path/length/hash,
  materializes the whole packet and deletes the file in `finally`.
- `PluginRuntimeServiceClient.kt:331`: packet read/decode runs on the existing
  response executor, then publishes the decoded result through the main handler.

Consequently, the trace's262144-byte consumer chunks are not evidence that the
upstream runtime delivered an incremental body. Adding another packet file
without changing the body-delivery contract would retain the whole-body seam.

## Candidate boundaries

| Delivery | Preserves source client | Body availability | Required lifecycle work |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Existing binary fallback | Yes | Complete body | Current implemented path |
| Source-owned sealed body file | Yes | After source production and verification | Explicit body lease, physical read lifetime, cancellation, cleanup |
| Source-owned live stream/pipe | Yes, if producer stays source-owned | Incremental only when source/interceptors permit | Producer and consumer completion, backpressure, cancellation drain, process death |
| Host replay from URL/headers alone | Not proven for WNACG | Ordinary host response | Insufficient proof of custom client semantics |

The assessment's design recommendation was a source-owned encoded-body capability in the
existing invocation protocol. Establish a sealed body-file lease first; permit
an incremental producer only after its source capability and physical lifetime
are proven. Reuse existing invocation, private-path/integrity checks and cleanup
authority. Do not create a second cache, runtime queue or network transport.

The body must have explicit framing and integrity distinct from the IPC envelope.
Never pass a `.packet` path directly to a decoder or treat it as a READY artifact.
The transport reference stays transient; the persistent Mihon locator, payload
revision, DownloadId and cache/trust authority remain the existing ones.

## Mandatory implementation gates

1. The existing source client/interceptors/settings remain the request authority.
   Existing direct-host sources retain their current capability path. Unknown
   clients do not gain direct replay by class-name or request-shape guessing.
2. NetLane remains the only scheduling authority. TaskControl rank/cancellation
   remains observable at source plan, runtime invocation and physical body work.
   Publishing metadata or a lease does not mean cancelled work has exited.
3. A lease retires only after admitted physical reads exit. Cancellation closes
   producer/consumer resources and waits for their completion; replacement,
   process death, late replies and repeated disposal cannot leak or double-free.
4. Reader only observes Pipeline output. DownloadSession/DownloadJob keep encoded
   ingress, aggregation, partial and durable artifact authority. Native ingress
   stays independent of decode-held source locks. The7/3 and2/1 windows stay fixed.
5. Typed network/source/verification/cancellation failures retain existing retry
   and generation handoff. A body carrier adds no retry or eligibility policy.
6. For streaming, verify partial writes, stopped consumers and cancelled blocking
   I/O before allowing early publication. For a sealed file, verify declared
   length/hash, immutable body framing and source/payload/generation binding.
7. Test genuine WNACG custom behavior and nonempty Cookie/POST separately from
   plain-client direct HTTP and protocol-mismatch fallback. Measure source timing,
   UI allocation/copy, native ingress and physical presentation independently.

No speedup or reduction in the observed3.9s origin open is established here.
Venera `onResponse/modifyImage` may require complete input; a body lease must not
pretend those transformations are incremental or bypass their owner.
